questions.enonce_markdown:
Two types of network is client\\server and peer-to-peer.

(a) Describe a client\\server network. (2 marks)

(b) Give TWO advantages of a peer-to-peer network. (2 marks)

(c) Give ONE disadvantage of client\\server network. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Client/server network (2 marks)**

In a client/server network one or more **powerful central computers (servers)** provide **services and resources** (file storage, printing, e-mail, databases, user authentication and security) to **many client computers (workstations)** that **send requests** to them. The users log in with accounts managed by the server, so **administration, backup and security are centralised**.

**(b) Two advantages of peer-to-peer (2 marks)**

- It is **cheap and easy to set up**: **no dedicated server and no network operating system** are needed, and no full-time network administrator.
- There is **no single point of failure**: if one computer is switched off the others keep working, and **every computer can share its files and printer directly** with the others (good for a small office or a home).

**(c) One disadvantage of client/server (1 mark)**

It is **expensive** (server hardware, network operating system licences, a skilled administrator) and **if the server fails the services are unavailable to every client**; the server can also become congested when many clients request it at the same time.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the function of each of the following:

(a) Router. (2 marks)

(b) Network Interface Card. (2 marks)

(c) Firmware. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Router (2 marks)**

A router **connects two or more different networks** (for example a school LAN to the Internet). It **reads the destination IP address of each packet** and, using its **routing table**, **forwards it along the best path** towards the destination; it usually also provides DHCP, NAT and a firewall for the LAN.

**(b) Network interface card (NIC) (2 marks)**

The NIC is the **adapter that lets a computer be connected to a network**. It **converts the data of the computer into signals suited to the medium (cable or radio) and back**, controls the **access to the medium**, and carries a **unique hardware (MAC) address** that identifies the computer on the LAN.

**(c) Firmware (2 marks)**

Firmware is **software stored permanently in the ROM or flash memory of a hardware device** (BIOS of a computer, a router, a printer, a phone). It **contains the basic instructions that control the device and start it up**, and it can be **updated** ("flashed") when the manufacturer releases a new version.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe utility software and give an example. (2 marks)

(b) Explain TWO roles of the operating system in managing processes. (2 marks)

(c) Differentiate between icon driven and command driven operating system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Utility software (2 marks)**

Utility software is **system software that carries out maintenance and housekeeping tasks** to keep the computer working well and secure (it is not used to produce documents but to **look after the system and its files**). **Example: an antivirus program** (which detects and removes malware); others are a disk defragmenter, a backup tool, a file-compression program (WinZip) and a disk clean-up tool.

**(b) Two roles in managing processes (2 marks)**

- **Scheduling**: the OS **decides which process uses the CPU, and for how long** (time slices, priorities), so that several programs seem to run at the same time (**multitasking**).
- **Resource allocation and control**: it **allocates memory and input/output devices** to each process, **creates and ends processes**, **handles interrupts** and prevents **conflicts and deadlock** between processes.

**(c) Icon driven and command driven systems (2 marks)**

| Icon driven (graphical user interface) | Command driven (command line interface) |
|---|---|
| The user **clicks or touches icons, windows and menus** with a pointing device. | The user **types commands** at a prompt. |
| **Easy to learn** for beginners, nothing to memorise; needs **more memory and processing power** (Windows, Android). | The **commands and their syntax must be memorised**; **fast and flexible for experts**, uses **little memory** (MS-DOS, Linux terminal). |
